about: The scripts of the snapshot (Checks/language/snapshot.js, entry W3.1-bis.2, item 11): every script of the folders below, run or skipped with its reason. A script of these folders that this file does not name stops the snapshot, and so does an entry whose script is gone.

An entry: script (a path from the root; a folder with a trailing slash is a compiled program), then either run: true or skip: the reason. Optional: args ({TEMP} is a fresh temporary folder), needs (files that must exist before anything runs), todo (it reads the TODO: TODO_MD is set), varies_with (what its counts also depend on outside the tree: todo, head, or a file), volatile_lines (lines whose numbers are not counts, each with its reason), probe and program (a compiled probe, run only with --with-probes), timeout_s.

entries.skip: downloads Installer.exe from a draft release of the repository with gh: it needs a release candidate, a tag and a token, and runs only in installer-smoke.yml

runs a downloaded Installer.exe against a stand-in for SOLIDWORKS and, with -Clients discover, against the profile of whoever runs it: it refuses off a throw-away machine, and runs only in installer-smoke.yml
without --self-test it drives SOLIDWORKS through the bridge and the ChangeByHand probe

needs dist/Installer.exe (a full build.ps1), and it installs, verifies and uninstalls some forty times in a temporary folder (about a minute); since H19 it does not attach to SOLIDWORKS unless given --attach (OCE_NO_ATTACH)

builds the installer (build.ps1, which needs SOLIDWORKS and rewrites dist/) and creates or updates a DRAFT release on GitHub: an action outside this machine; its -DryRun prints the plan, and Checks/check-workflow.ps1 reads the script for anything that could publish
prepares a release: runs build.ps1 (which rewrites Tools/catalog.json and dist/), fetches origin and runs the contract suite, which starts the bridge; it stops on an uncommitted tree by design
rebuilds the tracked Tests/data/obsolete-api-members.tsv from the SOLIDWORKS help extracted outside the repository: it writes a tracked file, and its input is not here
needs a version, and builds that old library in a git worktree under the temporary folder: a tool for the history, not a check of the tree
sets core.hooksPath in the configuration of the clone: it changes the clone and checks nothing
a module the TODO probes require, not a script: run alone it prints nothing and checks nothing

the pre-push hook: git runs it on push, and what it runs is in this registry one by one (the workflow check, the TODO probes, zero-or-unknown.js --self-test, the self-tests, the language gate, the publishability check)
without --check it edits the detector, the lexicon and the CI step in the working tree, one mutation at a time, and runs the contract suite once per mutation (about a minute each)
pushes throw-away branches to GitHub (with --no-verify) and runs the CI on them: an action outside this machine
